evals.name: solo-long-task-setup
evals.prompt: I'm about to refactor the auth module across ~8 files, run the test suite, then split it into three PRs. This'll take a while and I don't want to lose my place if the context gets cleared. Set me up.
evals.expected_output: Creates plan.md / in-progress.md / done.md at the repo root (gitignored), writes the phased plan with a RESUME HERE marker, and starts logging the live step to in-progress.md. No subagents.md — there is no fleet.

evals.name: coordinate-subagents-across-worktrees
evals.prompt: I'm coordinating three subagents, each on its own branch in a separate worktree under .worktrees/, to build features x/y/z in parallel. How do I track them so I can recover one if it dies mid-task like happened last time?
evals.expected_output: Sets up a coordinator-owned subagents.md registry (agentId/task/branch/worktree/status), explains the running->stalled recovery trigger, and that each subagent keeps its own plan/in-progress/done in its worktree; recovery walks the worktree column, reading the subagent's execution ledger (.superpowers/sdd/progress.md if it runs SDD, else in-progress.md).

evals.name: shared-repo-no-clobber
evals.prompt: Two of us plus a couple of agents are all hacking on the same repo today. Last time our note files kept clobbering each other. What's the discipline so that doesn't happen?
evals.expected_output: Recommends one worktree per actor as the primary answer (isolation by construction); if a shared tree is unavoidable, per-actor '## @<actor-id>' section ownership with edit-only-your-own-section and append-only done.md.

evals.name: recover-dead-subagent
evals.prompt: One of my background subagents just errored out with an API disconnect. It was halfway through something in a worktree. Can I recover what it was doing?
evals.expected_output: Runs the recovery runbook: read subagents.md, find the stalled row, cd to its worktree, read its execution ledger (.superpowers/sdd/progress.md if it ran SDD, else in-progress.md) + plan.md + done.md, check git status/log, then resume/harvest/abandon.

evals.name: one-off-question-no-trigger
evals.prompt: Quick one — what's the difference between Enum.map and Enum.each in Elixir?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger the skill — a one-off question, no multi-step session or coordination. Answer directly.

evals.name: below-bar-two-file-edit-no-trigger
evals.prompt: Rename the function `fetch_user/1` to `get_user/1` in lib/accounts/users.ex and update its one caller in lib/accounts/session.ex, then run that test file.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger the skill — a quick ~2-file edit with no subagents, no worktrees, and no second actor. It sits well below the multi-actor / subagent-dispatch / multi-worktree headline bar; just make the edits directly. Creating planning files here would bureaucratize a one-liner.
